name: Yosemite National Park
blurb: Snowmelt meadows, oaks and sequoias, with deer feeding cougars and bears.

tip.title: Shrink the snowpack
tip.text: Snowmelt waters the meadows. Set Snowpack & snowmelt to -100% and watch the meadow plants, then the deer, marmots and pikas that graze them, and the predators above.

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Yosemite National Park, American black bear, Mule deer). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: Grows in a few Yosemite groves, including Mariposa. Fire heat opens its cones and clears seedbeds, and decades of fire suppression have limited regeneration.
A mid-elevation oak whose acorns were a staple for Indigenous peoples and feed deer, bears and woodpeckers.
A high-elevation pine whose seeds feed Clark's nutcrackers. It is declining from blister rust, pine beetles and fire suppression.
Fireweed and other green meadow plants feed deer, marmots and pikas. Meadows are the grazing ground herbivores and their predators gather around.
Browses shrubs and trees and eats forbs and acorns. A main prey of cougars and sometimes bears and coyotes.
Eats grasses, leaves and flowers in summer, then hibernates for about eight months. Whistles an alarm when coyotes or eagles appear.
Stores plants as haypiles under talus. Killed by heat above roughly 25 C, so an early warning species for climate change.
Active all year and gnaws sequoia cone scales, knocking seeds loose. Also a prey item for bobcats.
Feeds mainly on pine seeds and buries surplus caches, making it the main disperser of whitebark pine.
Stores acorns in tree holes and eats insects. Recorded often around the oak woodlands.

nodes.name: American black bear
nodes.desc: Mostly plants such as berries, shoots and acorns, plus insects, carrion and deer fawns. Park managers use bear-proof food storage.
A generalist hunter of rodents, marmots and sometimes deer, also feeding on carrion.
Hunts squirrels, rodents, birds and occasionally deer fawns in the lower forests.
Hunts ground squirrels, marmots and other small mammals and birds from the air.
An opportunistic bird that scavenges carrion and scraps and takes eggs and small animals.

nodes.name: Cougar
nodes.desc: The park top predator, favouring large prey and mainly mule deer. Bears sometimes visit its kills.
Winter snow melts through spring and feeds the Merced and Tuolumne rivers and meadows. Snowpack is shrinking and melting earlier.
Drives growth through the short dry summer. Most precipitation falls in winter.
Lightning and past Indigenous burning cleared brush. Sequoias need fire to release seeds and clear seedbeds.

nodes.name: Fungi & soil decomposers
nodes.desc: Break down fallen needles, wood, carcasses and droppings and return nutrients to the soil.

story: Yosemite covers 1,187 square miles of granite cliffs, waterfalls, giant sequoia groves, lakes and glaciers, and has been a World Heritage Site since 1984. Records show nutcrackers eating whitebark pine, deer eating fireweed, and black bears, coyotes and cougars eating deer.
matters: About four million people visit each year, most staying in the valley's seven square miles. The park is still recognized for its biological diversity.
